tests/test_helpers_ok.py:86-89: the decorator-factory helper def test(name) will be collected as a test and error.
pytest's default python_functions = test is a prefix match, so a module-level function named exactly test is collected.
The repo has no pytest config that would change this.
pytest then treats name as a fixture request, finds no such fixture, and reports fixture 'name' not found as an error at setup.
The file's docstring says it holds correct tests that only look suspicious, so a fixture error is a real defect in it. Any pytest run over tests/ will report it.
The fix is to rename the helper so it doesn't start with test, for example deco_factory. Alternatively, set test = False on it or move it out of the collected path.

1 issue found (bug), validated:

src/cart.py:5 cart_total sums floats with no rounding, so totals shown to the customer carry float noise. Executed in the workspace: cart_total([0.1, 0.2]) returns 0.30000000000000004; cart_total([19.99, 5.01, 0.1]) returns 25.099999999999998; notify(sender, that total) sends 'Your total is 0.30000000000000004'. apply_discount rounds to 2 places (line 11) but cart_total does not, so the two money functions disagree. Every test uses ints only (tests/test_cart.py:7-23, tests/test_helpers_ok.py:10-29), so nothing covers decimal prices. A cart with prices [19.99, 5.01, 0.1] gives 25.099999999999998. notify() puts that string in the customer message. Comparing it to an expected 25.10 total also fails.

tests/test_helpers_ok.py:82 test_inline_skip_with_reason calls pytest.skip() unconditionally at the top, so the assert below it is dead code and the test can never pass or fail. The test always reports as skipped. The cart_total([1]) == 1 assertion never executes, so it can never catch a regression. The skip should be a decorator or sit behind a real condition, such as a missing payment provider.
The weak assertions in tests/test_cart.py are the planted defects the fixture exists to hold. They are intended, so I did not report them as bugs.

tests/test_cart.py:36 test_total_type asserts isinstance(cart_total([1]), int), which pins an implementation detail and passes for the wrong reason. cart_total is sum(prices), so it returns a float for float prices. That would break any caller using prices like 19.99. The test only checks the int case and breaks if the function legitimately switches to Decimal or float. It guards no behavior a user cares about.

src/cart.py:11 apply_discount and cart_total do no type or sign validation, and the discount uses float math then round. A negative total, a non-numeric percent, or NaN gives a surprising result. apply_discount(100, float('nan')) passes both comparisons (both are False) and returns nan. Float rounding (round(x, 2) banker's rounding) can be off by a cent for monetary values. Decimal would be safer.
